articles.title: Chuva forte causa queda de árvores e falta de energia no Sul de Minas | G1
articles.standfirst: Andradas e Cambuí registraram ocorrências neste sábado (10). Não houve feridos nem desabrigados, segundo as Defesas Civis.
articles.summary: Andradas e Cambuí registraram ocorrências neste sábado (10). Não houve feridos nem desabrigados, segundo as Defesas Civis.
articles.body:
Uma chuva forte provocou estragos em cidades do Sul de Minas neste sábado (10). Em Andradas (MG), houve queda de árvores e galhos, postes e um outdoor arrancados, além de danos a dois carros. Já em Cambuí (MG), foram registradas quedas de árvores e alagamentos em ruas e rodovias. Segundo as Defesas Civis dos municípios, não houve feridos nem desabrigados.

Temporal provoca quedas de árvores e danos em Andradas (MG) — Foto: Defesa Civil

Em Andradas, a chuva forte que atingiu a cidade no sábado (10) provocou quedas de árvores e galhos, postes e um outdoor arrancados, além de danos a dois carros. Segundo a Defesa Civil, quase todas as praças tiveram registros de queda de galhos.

Entre os locais atingidos estão as praças Coronel Antônio Augusto de Oliveira, Doutor Alcides Mosconi e Doutor Luiz Venturelli. Também houve ocorrências na Avenida Bias Fortes, na Vila Caracol e no Jardim de Areta.

Na Praça Doutor Alcides Mosconi, no entorno da Igreja Matriz, uma árvore caiu sobre dois carros. Os veículos foram retirados do local e tiveram danos considerados superficiais, segundo a Defesa Civil.

A tempestade também provocou interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica em vários pontos do município, principalmente na região central. Segundo a Cemig, a intensidade da chuva e dos ventos causou quedas de árvores e o lançamento de objetos, como partes de telhados e galhos, contra a rede elétrica, provocando curtos-circuitos e rompimentos de cabos.

As equipes da companhia trabalham desde o início das ocorrências para restabelecer o serviço. Cerca de 300 clientes permaneciam sem energia neste domingo (11), e a previsão era de que o fornecimento fosse normalizado gradativamente ao longo do dia.

Até o último levantamento da Defesa Civil, não havia registro de feridos ou desabrigados no município.

Em Cambuí, uma árvore caiu na Rua Antônio Dias de Medeiros, no bairro Portal Monte Verde, na tarde deste sábado.

A chuva também provocou alagamentos em diferentes pontos da cidade, incluindo trechos da MG-295, da Rodovia Fernão Dias e da Rua Joaquim Augusto da Cunha.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, foram registrados 10 milímetros de chuva durante a tarde. Até o balanço divulgado pelo órgão, ninguém havia ficado ferido ou desabrigado em decorrência das ocorrências.

articles.title: Furto em hamburgueria em Teresópolis: vídeo mostra ação de homem | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmeras de segurança registraram toda a ação no estabelecimento em Teresópolis. Suspeito ainda procurou outros objetos de valor antes de fugir.
articles.summary: Imagens de segurança mostram o momento em que um suspeito invade o comércio em Teresópolis, leva dinheiro e celular, e foge após vasculhar o local.
articles.body:
As câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que um homem quebra a porta de uma hamburgueria, em Teresópolis, na Região Serrana do Rio. Na madrugada deste domingo (11) ele entra no estabelecimento, vai até as gavetas e furta o dinheiro do caixa e um celular. Antes de fugir, ainda procura outros objetos de valor e coloca o material levado dentro de uma sacola.

Nas imagens, o homem aparece usando boné e carregando uma sacola plástica nas costas. Depois de entrar no comércio, ele circula pelo local e abre as gavetas em busca de outros objetos. Em seguida, esconde o que encontrou dentro da bolsa e deixa o estabelecimento

Segundo os proprietários da hamburgueria, o furto aconteceu durante a madrugada. As imagens das câmeras de segurança devem ajudar na identificação do suspeito.

Informações que possam ajudar a polícia a localizar o suspeito podem ser repassadas ao Disque Denúncia pelo telefone (21) 2253-1177. O anonimato é garantido.

O suspeito usava um boné e carregava uma sacola plástica nas costas. Ele circulou pelo comércio abrindo gavetas em busca de objetos de valor. — Foto: Redes sociais

articles.summary: O Burning Fest Praia Grande oferece churrasco, hambúrgueres e shows gratuitos de rock no Pavilhão Jair Rodrigues durante o feriado de 12 de outubro.
articles.body:
O Burning Fest chega ao último dia nesta segunda-feira (12), em Praia Grande, no litoral de São Paulo, com churrasco, entrada e estacionamento gratuitos e três shows de rock. O festival gastronômico funciona das 12h às 22h.

O evento acontece em frente ao Pavilhão de Eventos Jair Rodrigues, na Rua Savério Fittipaldi, s/nº, no bairro Quietude. O espaço conta com área infantil e permite a entrada de animais de estimação.

O último dia terá apresentações de Perdidos no Espaço, com rock nacional, às 13h; Cólica Renal, em tributo ao Mamonas Assassinas, às 17h; e Keep The Faith, em tributo ao Bon Jovi, às 20h.

O festival reúne mestres churrasqueiros e diferentes técnicas de preparo, com opções como costelão fogo de chão, carnes assadas e defumadas, hambúrgueres artesanais, acompanhamentos, sobremesas e chopp.

Festival de churrasco Burning Fest ocorre em Praia Grande (SP) até segunda (10) — Foto: Divulgação/Redes Sociais

A programação musical começou na sexta-feira (9), com a Let There Be Rock, banda cover do AC/DC. No sábado (10), se apresentaram Urban Chilli, com rock nacional, Danger, em tributo ao KISS, e Deep Illusion, em homenagem ao Guns N’ Roses.

No domingo (11), o público contou com Confisco, tributo ao Charlie Brown Jr., Calando Brabo, com o chamado rock do sertão, e Lost Dogs, em tributo ao Pearl Jam.

articles.title: Incêndio em subestação de energia de Salvador é finalizado | G1
articles.standfirst: Situação aconteceu em Amaralina e afeta outras localidades no Caminho das Árvores e Pituba. Causa do fogo ainda não foi determinada.
articles.summary: Situação aconteceu em Amaralina e afeta outras localidades no Caminho das Árvores e Pituba. Causa do fogo ainda não foi determinada
articles.body:
O incêndio que atingiu a subestação de energia elétrica do bairro de Amaralina , em Salvador , foi apagado, após cerca de três horas de trabalho dos bombeiros militares. A informação foi divulgada pela Corporação.

Apesar disso, segundo a Neoenergia Coelba, o fornecimento ainda não havia sido restabelecido em 100% dos locais afetados, até a última atualização desta reportagem. Entre os pontos que permanecem sem energia, está a Pituba.

Além do bairro e da própria Amaralina, outras localidades foram afetadas na região, como o Caminho das Árvores. Um vídeo feito por testemunhas durante a tarde mostra muita fumaça escura na subestação, localizado na Rua Visconde de Itaborahy.

Conforme apurou a TV Bahia, moradores ouviram uma explosão antes do fogo. Algumas pessoas chegaram a deixar suas casas temporariamente, por medo e por recomendação de segurança.

Ocorrência em subestação de energia deixa bairros de Salvador sem energia elétrica — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A via em frente à subestação precisou ser completamente interditada para os trabalho, com ajuda da Superintendência de Trânsito de Salvador (Transalvador). Os motoristas que costumam transitar na região precisaram buscar outras alternativas.

Em nota, o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar da Bahia (CBM-BA) informou que ao chegarem ao local, os agentes identificaram estampidos provocados por curtos-circuitos no interior da estrutura.

Como técnicos da concessionária já estavam presentes, a guarnição efetuou o isolamento preventivo da área e aguardou o desligamento total da rede elétrica para dar início ao combate direto às chamas.

Com o fim do risco aos bombeiros, eles avançaram nas linhas de combate até a extinção completa de todos os focos de incêndio. A operação foi concluída com sucesso às 17h14. A causa das chamas, no entanto, ainda não foram determinadas.

articles.title: Professora é afastada após denúncia de agressão em São Tomé das Letras | G1
articles.standfirst: Mãe de menino de 7 anos afirma que o filho foi empurrado em sala de aula. Outra família relata episódio semelhante com uma aluna na semana anterior.
articles.summary: Mãe de menino de 7 anos afirma que o filho foi empurrado em sala de aula. Outra família relata episódio semelhante com uma aluna na semana anterior.
articles.body:
Uma professora foi afastada após uma denúncia de possível agressão contra um aluno da Escola Municipal Portal das Letras, em São Tomé das Letras (MG).

O suposto caso veio à tona depois que a mãe de um menino de 7 anos procurou a escola para pedir explicações sobre uma situação que teria ocorrido dentro da sala de aula, na quarta-feira (7).

Segundo a costureira Michelle Cristiane Pinto, o filho foi entregar uma atividade à professora eventual, que substitui a docente responsável pela turma durante um período de licença, quando teria sido empurrado e caído.

“Pela manhã, eu estava arrumando o meu filho para ir para a escola, quando ele me abraçou pela cintura com o olho cheio de lágrima e me relatou que a professora havia o empurrado e ele caiu na cadeira. Eu fiquei assustada, fui perguntar, falei: 'meu filho, como assim? Você fez alguma coisa?' Mesmo se tivesse feito, não teria motivo para isso. É uma criança de 7 anos. E aí que ele foi me falar, ele falou: 'não mãe, ontem eu fui entregar a lição para a 'pro', ela pegou e me empurrou'.”, contou.

Escola Municipal Portal das Letras em São Tomé das Letras (MG) — Foto: Devanir Gino/EPTV

Uma mulher que estava na instituição para buscar o próprio filho afirmou ter presenciado o episódio.

"Quando cheguei na sala para pegar ele, as crianças fazendo bagunça, ela gritando com as crianças, nisso um aluno levantou para entregar um caderno, ele entregou, simplesmente jogou o caderno dele, empurrou ele, mandou ele sentar. Nisso eu peguei meu filho, perguntei para o professor do lado quem que era aquela professora, ela me falou quem era, nisso eu falei assim, então eu vou na diretoria", relatou a testemunha, que preferiu não se identificar.

Michelle disse que já havia ouvido relatos de crianças sobre comportamentos agressivos da professora, como gritos e batidas na mesa. Após conversar com o filho, ela foi até a escola para cobrar providências.

"Eu estou aguardando que a escola exonere e tome as medidas cabíveis, porque a gente vai tomar, a gente vai atrás do Ministério Público, a gente vai fazer o que for possível para que não fique impune essa situação", afirmou.

Professora é suspensa após denúncia de agressão contra aluno em São Tomé das Letras, MG — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

A mãe de outra estudante da turma, Laudiene Nascimento, afirmou que a filha também teria sofrido uma agressão atribuída à mesma professora, na semana anterior.

De acordo com Laudiene, a menina contou que foi entregar uma atividade à docente e teve a folha jogada contra o rosto.

"Ela chegou lá no almoço, ela já chega contando tudo para mim o que aconteceu, a comida que foi na escola, essas coisas. A gente pergunta e ela já começou contando. Ela chegou e falou para mim que foi entregar uma lição para a professora na mesa da professora e a professora jogou essa folha na cara dela, que pegou até no olho dela, ficou com o olho dolorido", contou.

Depois disso, a filha teria passado a demonstrar medo de voltar à escola e chegou a pedir para não frequentar as aulas.

"Se a professora era para ser uma mãe pra eles na sala, eles ficam com medo. Ela já começou a pedir para mim, pelo amor de Deus, mas não deixa eu ir", disse a dona de casa

A diretora da Escola Municipal Portal das Letras, Elaine Cristina de Castro, informou que a instituição está tomando as medidas necessárias para apurar as denúncias.

“A escola acolheu essa mãe, fizemos as devidas orientações que isso não aconteceria, que tomaríamos, como estamos tomando, as devidas providências em relação ao corrido. Toda e qualquer escola tem um prazo para resolver esse tipo de situação, porque todos os lados devem ser ouvidos e todos têm o direito à plena defesa”, declarou a diretora.

A EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo , procurou a professora para ouvir a versão dela, mas ela não quis se manifestar. A reportagem também tentou contato com a advogada da profissional, mas não conseguiu retorno.

articles.title: Vagas de emprego em Itapetininga: Atacarejo abre 118 postos | G1
articles.standfirst: Processo seletivo oferece vagas para chefes de seção, líderes, operadores e caixas. A previsão é de que a unidade seja inaugurada em novembro, na Vila Carolina.
articles.summary: Vagas de emprego em Itapetininga no novo Cash Atacado oferecem salários de até R$ 3.400 e benefícios para cargos de liderança, operação e caixa.
articles.body:
Unidade será instalada na Rua Benedita Silva Rosa, 43, na Vila Carolina, em uma via paralela à Avenida 5 de Novembro; processo seletivo está aberto — Foto: Prefeitura de Itapetininga/Divulgação

Itapetininga (SP) terá uma nova unidade da rede Cash Atacado, com previsão de inauguração em novembro. A instalação do empreendimento será na Vila Carolina.

Conforme a prefeitura, o processo seletivo já está aberto e oferece 118 oportunidades em diferentes áreas, incluindo chefes de seção, líderes, operadores e caixas. Os salários variam de R$ 2.124 a R$ 3.400, dependendo da função.

A nova unidade será instalada na Rua Benedita Silva Rosa, 43, em uma via paralela à Avenida 5 de Novembro.

Os interessados devem comparecer ao Posto de Atendimento ao Trabalhador (PAT) de Itapetininga com um documento oficial com foto.

A unidade fica na Rua Monsenhor Soares, 251, no Centro, e funciona de segunda a sexta-feira, das 9h às 17h, exceto feriados.

articles.title: Irmão de deputado morre afogado em praia de Fortaleza | G1
articles.standfirst: Valtenir Costa era irmão do parlamentar Nizo Costa (PT). O caso aconteceu na Praia da Sabiaguaba.
articles.summary: Valtenir Costa era irmão do parlamentar Nizo Costa (PT). O caso aconteceu na Praia da Sabiaguaba.
articles.body:
O empresário e agricultor Valtenir Costa, de 49 anos, morreu afogado, neste domingo (11), na Praia da Sabiaguaba, em Fortaleza . Ele era irmão do deputado estadual Nizo Costa (PT). Valtenir estava a passeio em Fortaleza com a família para aproveitar o feriadão.

Valtenir estava na praia com a mãe, irmãos, esposa, filho, sobrinhos e cunhados. O Corpo de Bombeiros informou que o afogamento ocorreu por trás da barreira de pedras da praia, em ponto cego da torre de guarda-vidas, no lado oposto ao Rio Cocó em relação ao Posto de Guarda-Vidas 11.

A população avistou o afogamento e sinalizaram para a guarnição, que atravessou o rio com pranchões e chegou rapidamente ao local. Os bombeiros informaram que o empresário, quando foi socorrido, estava com sinais de maior gravidade devido ao afogamento, como respiração com muita espuma.

Ainda na praia, Valtenir teve uma parada cardíaca. A morte dele foi confirmada por uma equipe do Samu que atendeu a ocorrência.

Valtenir era natural de Tarrafas , no interior do estado, e morava no distrito de São Sebastião, em Cariús , no Centro-Sul do Ceará. Roberto Filho, prefeito de Iguatu (município da mesma região) , é amigo do deputado Nizo Costa e lamentou a morte.

“Neste momento de dor e despedida, manifesto meus mais sinceros sentimentos a toda a família e aos amigos. Que Deus conceda força e conforte o coração de cada um para enfrentar essa perda”, disse Roberto Filho.

articles.title: Atletas de Divinópolis podem solicitar apoio para transporte | G1
articles.standfirst: Cadastro da SEMEJ segue até 31 de outubro e é voltado a atletas e equipes com competições fora do município previstas até junho de 2027.
articles.summary: Cadastro da SEMEJ segue até 31 de outubro e é voltado a atletas e equipes com competições fora do município previstas até junho de 2027.
articles.body:
Atletas e equipes esportivas de Divinópolis podem receber apoio no transporte para competições realizadas fora do município. Os interessados que tenham competições previstas até junho de 2027 devem cadastrar propostas para participar do processo de seleção da Secretaria Municipal de Esportes e Juventude (SEMEJ).

O prazo para cadastramento segue até 31 de outubro. A iniciativa tem como objetivo antecipar as demandas dos atletas e equipes, permitindo que a SEMEJ conheça o calendário de competições, analise as solicitações e planeje a utilização dos recursos disponíveis.

Podem participar atletas residentes em Divinópolis e equipes formadas por moradores do município, de diferentes modalidades esportivas. As propostas podem ser relacionadas à participação em competições, campeonatos, torneios, eventos e outras atividades de representação esportiva previstas no Programa de Apoio ao Esporte.

Atletas individuais devem preencher o Requerimento de Auxílio Financeiro – Formulário Padrão Atleta Individual do Programa de Apoio ao Esporte , com dados pessoais, informações esportivas e detalhes da competição.

No caso das equipes, deve ser preenchido o Requerimento de Auxílio Financeiro – Equipe/Clube , com a identificação do responsável técnico, modalidade, competição e relação dos integrantes que participarão do deslocamento.

Também é necessário preencher o Projeto para Solicitação de Auxílio do Programa de Apoio ao Esporte Amador , com informações que permitam à secretaria analisar a proposta.

O projeto deve apresentar dados sobre o atleta ou equipe, modalidade, categoria, competição, organização responsável, cidade e estado onde será realizada, além do período do evento.

O documento também deve explicar a finalidade da participação, a importância da competição para o desenvolvimento esportivo e a necessidade do apoio para o transporte.

Para participar da seleção, é necessário apresentar:

Requerimento de Auxílio Financeiro do Programa de Apoio ao Esporte, de acordo com a modalidade de participação, individual ou equipe;

Documento oficial de identificação, como RG ou CNH, com CPF. No caso de equipes, a documentação deve ser apresentada para todos os atletas participantes;

Comprovante de residência em Divinópolis/MG. Para equipes, deve ser apresentado o comprovante de todos os integrantes;

Documento que comprove a condição de representante ou responsável legal, quando o atleta for menor de idade. Se o responsável for pai ou mãe, basta apresentar o documento de identificação;

Comprovante de participação na competição, como convite, convocação, inscrição, regulamento, programação oficial ou documento equivalente;

Projeto de solicitação de auxílio, devidamente preenchido, com informações sobre o evento, deslocamento, distância, custos e demais dados solicitados;

Documentação do técnico ou instrutor, com registro no CREF-MG ou documentos que comprovem experiência e atuação na área esportiva.

A apresentação da documentação do técnico ou instrutor é obrigatória. Todos os requerimentos e documentos devem ser enviados para o e-mail viagenssemej@divinopolis.mg.gov.br.

As propostas serão analisadas pela SEMEJ à medida que forem recebidas. Não será necessário aguardar o fim do período de cadastramento para o início da avaliação.

Cada solicitação será submetida à análise e julgamento, considerando os critérios do Programa de Apoio ao Esporte, a documentação apresentada, as características da competição e a disponibilidade orçamentária e financeira do município.

A inscrição não garante automaticamente a concessão do auxílio para transporte. O benefício dependerá do atendimento aos requisitos, da análise da proposta e da disponibilidade de recursos.

Por isso, atletas e equipes que já tenham competições programadas são orientados a encaminhar a documentação com antecedência, sem esperar a proximidade do evento.

articles.title: Russia strikes power plant in Ukraine after Trump announces energy ceasefire
articles.summary: A thermal power plant was struck at least twice, Ukrainian officials said.
articles.body:
Russia has attacked a power plant in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kharkiv despite President Donald Trump's statement earlier Sunday that both sides had agreed to an "energy ceasefire," according to Ukrainian officials.

A local official told ABC News the thermal power plant CHP-5 was struck at least twice, causing a fire. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a statement confirmed Russia had attacked the plant, as well as another in Kyiv, saying it had taken place after Trump's announcement.

Announcing the energy ceasefire earlier on social media, Trump said both Russia and Ukraine had agreed and that it would immediately come into effect, but Zelenskyy has said Ukraine was caught off guard by the announcement. Russia has yet to comment.

"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump's post said.

Zelenskyy was surprised by Trump's announcement and only learned about it from social media, a senior source in Ukraine's presidential office told ABC News. Ukraine, however, was ready to accept it immediately if Russia agrees, Zelenskyy said.

Shortly before Trump's declaration, Zelenskyy told Jon Karl on "This Week" that Ukraine wanted an immediate "energy ceasefire" that would see it stop striking Russian oil refineries provided the Kremlin halted attacks on Ukraine's power infrastructure.

Zelenskyy, in his evening address, said Ukraine is "ready not to strike at Russian energy, and we are counting on Russia's similar readiness."

"Ukraine has proposed many de-escalation steps," Zelenskyy said. "Ukraine wants peace. The question is whether Russia wants it."

articles.title: ICE agent strikes man with car during pursuit in Texas, authorities say
articles.summary: The injured man was identified as Miguel Parra-Hernandez, officials said.
articles.body:
A man was hospitalized after he was struck by a vehicle driven by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent who was allegedly pursuing him and another man on Saturday, Texas law enforcement officials and ICE said.

Maj. Anthony McConnell of the Harris County Sheriff's Office's Special Investigation Bureau told reporters that around 7:20 a.m. local time, law enforcement officers were called to Clay Road near Highway 6 just outside Houston after the unidentified ICE agent called 911 for an ambulance for the man, later identified by ICE as Miguel Parra-Hernandez, who was struck.

An ICE spokesperson said in a statement that the agency was attempting to arrest another man, Jose Mendoza-Cervantes, a Mexican national who they allege had a criminal record and a final order of removal by a judge.

The ICE agent allegedly observed Mendoza-Cervantes and Parra-Hernandez, who the agency alleged was undocumented, enter a car and attempted a car stop, according to ICE.

McConnell said the ICE agent allegedly was pursuing the man and another person in their car and during the chase, the driver and the passenger left their vehicle on foot.

Surveillance video of the incident reviewed by ABC News appears to show the agent maneuvering his vehicle in the direction of the man running and striking him with the vehicle.

ICE alleged in a statement that "Parra-Hernandez ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck."

Parra-Hernandez appeared to suffer a broken leg, McConnell said. He was taken to the hospital and is in ICE custody, according to ICE.

ICE didn't immediately list any criminal history about Parra-Hernandez.

McConnell referred further inquiries about the incident to ICE.

"We're here to investigate the crash," he told reporters.

Deputies were collecting video evidence from nearby buildings as part of their investigation, McConnell said. No arrests have been made.

Mendoza-Cervantes was not found as of Sunday afternoon, ICE said.

Family members of Parra-Hernandez, community leaders and officials of the immigration FIEL Houston held a news conference in Houston on Sunday.

"We have been in contact with Miguel's family, and they are very worried about his health. He is alive but is supposed to undergo surgery for his leg, which is broken in three places," said Cesar Espinosa, executive director at FIEL Houston.

Espinosa demanded accountability from ICE and called for a transparent investigation of the incident.

"We have more questions than answers. The biggest question we have is why does this keep happening? We demand answers and transparency from all agencies involved," Espinosa said.

Harris County Precinct 4 Commissioner Lesley Briones called on ICE to provide all evidence to the Harris County Sheriff's office and to cooperate with the investigation, adding that she was "horrified" about the incident.

"We demand full transparency, accountability, and respect for the rule of law," she said in her statement.

Harris County Attorney Abbie Kamin said, "Time is of the essence in getting the facts, and the public deserves clear, accurate answers."

"ICE must cooperate fully with the local investigation," Kamin said. "My office supports Sheriff Ed Gonzalez and District Attorney Sean Teare in their ongoing independent investigation, and the Harris County Attorney's Office stands ready to assist and support these critical efforts. We will continue to monitor developments closely as the facts become clear."

The Texas incident comes two days after ICE agents shot a man inside his car with his 5-year-old son in the backseat in New York City during an attempted arrest.

Oscar Belgal, 28, is currently being held in custody and awaiting court appearances following the incident.

ICE alleged Belgal, a Dominican national, "weaponized his vehicle," and rammed ICE vehicles. Surveillance footage released by the police showed the initial encounter where two armed men approached Belgal's car and hit the driver side window.

Several New York City officials, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani, condemned ICE's actions and called on the federal government to remove them from the city.

articles.title: Feriado de Nossa Senhora no DF terá missas na Catedral e show com Frei Gilson; veja detalhes | G1
articles.standfirst: Catedral Metropolitana de Brasília, cartão-postal da cidade, recebe o nome da Padroeira do Brasil. Novena começou na semana passada; missa principal será às 17h de segunda.
articles.summary: Catedral Metropolitana de Brasília, cartão-postal da cidade, recebe o nome da Padroeira do Brasil. Novena começou na semana passada; missa principal será às 17h de segunda.
articles.body:
Catedral de Brasília, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: TV Globo

Fiéis de todo o país celebram, nesta segunda-feira (12) o dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, padroeira do Brasil – e de Brasília , desde a fundação da capital.

A data terá programação especial organizada pela Arquidiocese de Brasília, com atividades religiosas e atrações para toda a família na Esplanada dos Ministérios e na Catedral Metropolitana.

Além das celebrações religiosas, a programação contará com espaço infantil e parque de brinquedos infláveis para as crianças.

7h – Corrida da Padroeira, com pelotão dos padres

9h – Missa das crianças, celebrada por Dom Ricardo Hoepers

17h – Missa solene de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, presidida pelo cardeal Paulo Cezar Costa e todo o clero

Encerrando as comemorações, o Frei Gilson fará um show gratuito em palco montado na Esplanada dos Ministérios. Para participar, basta doar 1 kg de alimento não perecível.

Realizada pela Arquidiocese de Brasília desde 1960, a celebração de Nossa Senhora Aparecida é uma das mais tradicionais festas religiosas do Distrito Federal. A ligação da santa com a capital, porém, começou antes mesmo da inauguração da cidade.

Em maio de 1957, durante a primeira missa celebrada em Brasília, ainda em construção, uma imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida foi entregue à futura capital pelo então arcebispo de São Paulo, cardeal Carlos Carmelo de Vasconcelos Motta.

A imagem, réplica da que está no Santuário Nacional de Aparecida (SP), percorreu todas as capitais brasileiras antes de chegar ao Distrito Federal.

Catedral de Brasília em fase de conclusão. — Foto: Revista Brasília/Arquivo Público do DF

A relação foi fortalecida em 1960, quando o papa São João XXIII determinou, por meio da bula de criação da Arquidiocese de Brasília, que ela fosse colocada sob a proteção de Nossa Senhora Aparecida. Dois anos depois, a santa foi oficialmente proclamada padroeira da arquidiocese.

Em 1970, com a inauguração da Catedral Metropolitana de Brasília, a imagem passou a ocupar lugar de destaque no interior do templo.

A devoção a Nossa Senhora Aparecida teve início em 1717, quando três pescadores encontraram, nas águas do Rio Paraíba do Sul, em São Paulo, uma imagem da santa partida em duas partes.

Segundo a tradição católica, após recolherem os fragmentos da imagem, os pescadores conseguiram uma pesca abundante, episódio considerado o primeiro milagre atribuído à santa.

Ao longo dos séculos, Nossa Senhora Aparecida tornou-se um dos maiores símbolos da fé católica no país. Em 1929, o papa Pio XI declarou oficialmente Nossa Senhora Aparecida padroeira do Brasil. A proclamação solene ocorreu no ano seguinte, no Rio de Janeiro, então capital federal.

O dia 12 de outubro foi transformado em feriado nacional em 1980, durante a visita do papa João Paulo II ao Brasil.

Evento da imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida no Rio de Janeiro, em 1931. — Foto: Centro de Doc. e Memória Santuário de Aparecida

articles.title: China impõe sanções a ministros do Paraguai e de Belize. | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida tem caráter simbólico e proíbe entrada das autoridades no país; Paraguai e Belize estão entre as 12 únicas nações que ainda mantêm laços diplomáticos com a ilha.
articles.summary: Medida tem caráter simbólico e proíbe entrada das autoridades no país; Paraguai e Belize estão entre as 12 únicas nações que ainda mantêm laços diplomáticos com a ilha.
articles.body:
Vista de prédios comerciais e residenciais de Taipei, em Taiwan, no dia 12 de maio de 2026 — Foto: Ann Wang/Reuters

A China impôs sanções nesta segunda-feira (12) ao ministro das Comunicações do Paraguai e ao ministro das Relações Exteriores de Belize devido às relações de seus países com Taiwan, território que Pequim reivindica como próprio.

Paraguai e Belize são dois dos apenas 12 países que mantêm relações diplomáticas formais com Taiwan. A China afirma que Taiwan é uma de suas províncias, sem direito aos atributos de um Estado, uma visão que o governo de Taipé rejeita veementemente.

As sanções são, em grande parte, simbólicas, uma vez que ministros de países aliados diplomaticamente a Taiwan geralmente não viajam para a China. Anteriormente, essas sanções haviam sido aplicadas principalmente a políticos ocidentais pelo apoio a Taiwan, que tem governo democrático.

Nem o Ministério de Tecnologias da Informação e Comunicação do Paraguai nem o Ministério das Relações Exteriores de Belize responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentários fora do horário comercial regular. O Ministério das Relações Exteriores de Taiwan não fez comentários imediatos.

O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China citou a soberania e a segurança nacional como motivos para as medidas, afirmando que alguns políticos de Belize e do Paraguai têm sido "anti-China" ao pressionar para que suas nações mantenham laços diplomáticos com Taiwan.

As medidas incluem a proibição de vistos de entrada para Hong Kong e Macau, além da proibição de que organizações e indivíduos chineses se envolvam em transações, cooperação ou outras atividades, afirmou o ministério em dois comunicados.

O ministro das Relações Exteriores de Belize, Francis Fonseca, encontrou-se com seu homólogo de Taiwan, Lin Chia-lung, em Belize no mês passado.

Em junho, o ministro de Tecnologias da Informação e Comunicação do Paraguai, Gustavo Villate, encontrou-se com o vice-ministro das Relações Exteriores de Taiwan, Chen Ming-chi, no Paraguai.

Pouco antes do anúncio chinês, a embaixada de Belize em Taiwan publicou em sua página no Facebook uma mensagem celebrando o aniversário de 11 de outubro, que marca o 37º ano desde que os dois países estabeleceram relações.

Taiwan: uma peça com potencial explosivo no tabuleiro China-EUA — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

"Juntos, esperamos um futuro de crescimento, oportunidades e amizade duradoura", escreveu a embaixada.

A China tem aumentado a pressão sobre os aliados diplomáticos restantes de Taiwan para que cortem os laços com Taipé.

O último país a fazer isso foi a pequena nação das Ilhas do Pacífico, Nauru, em 2024, enquanto, no ano anterior, Honduras encerrou suas relações de décadas com Taiwan.

articles.title: Boat disaster off Djibouti leaves at least 139 dead, with toll feared to rise
articles.summary: At least 139 people, including children, have died after a boat carrying more than 300 migrants capsized off the coast of Djibouti in east Africa, the International Organization for Migration said Sunday.
articles.body: At least 139 people, including children, have died after a boat carrying more than 300 migrants capsized off the coast of Djibouti in east Africa, the International Organization for Migration said Sunday. That number only includes those buried by authorities in Djibouti. Others have been buried by the migrants themselves but they won’t be added to the official count until authorities can verify the bodies, Alexandre Coissac, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti, told the AP via the phone. “What is terrible is that they were buried with no names, in a common grave, like in a war situation,” Coissac said. “They all have a mother, a father, and we may never learn what happened.” Coissac said the migrants boarded the ship in the evening of Oct. 8 and that it sank very soon after, close to the shore, “mainly because it was overcrowded.” “The local authorities did their best,” Coissac said, “but they were overwhelmed with all the bodies that kept coming at once towards the shore.” He said authorities were bringing the surviving migrants to the IOM rescue center in Obock where they receive medical assistance after swallowing sea water, and psychological support. “They’re all in a state of shock,” Coissac, who visited the area of the shipwreck Saturday, said. “I tried to talk to some of them but it’s very difficult.” Some of the migrants in the IOM center are already aware that their family members died during the shipwreck. Others were given access to phones to call loved ones back home to notify them they are alive. At least 84 people remained missing in one of the deadliest shipwrecks yet on the popular but perilous crossing from the Horn of Africa to the Arabian Peninsula, where many migrants seek work in rich Gulf nations. The boat was traveling from Djibouti to Yemen when it capsized on Thursday night or Friday morning, according to the IOM. More than 80 people survived, all of them Ethiopian nationals, it said. The Geneva-based UN migration agency said the vessel had 305 people on board and warned that the death toll could still rise. Personal items likely belonging to the migrants, including shoes, were seen on a beach in a video shared by IOM. Rescue work continued as fears grew for the missing. Tens of thousands of migrants from the Horn of Africa travel every year through Djibouti and across the Bab el-Mandeb Strait towards Gulf countries in search of safety and economic opportunities, the IOM said in its statement. That movement has continued despite newly escalating fighting in Yemen, on the other side of the strait. “This is a devastating loss of life,” said Coissac. “This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities.” In recent weeks, at least 2,000 Yemenis have received aid in Djibouti as the fighting has escalated in Yemen between the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government and Iranian-backed Houthi rebels. That’s the opposite direction from the movement of the migrants who died in the shipwreck and the typical migration patterns of recent years: The tens of thousands who cross from eastern Africa toward Yemen each year have typically been looking for work in places like Saudi Arabia. Over 900 migrants died or went missing along the route last year, according to IOM’s Missing Migrants Project. “No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way,” IOM Director-General Amy Pope said. “We cannot keep treating these deaths as normal. Safe and legal pathways save lives. I am asking governments and donors to act before the next boat goes down.”

articles.title: Ceuta or Sebta? Why one city has two names and a disputed status
articles.summary: Felipe VI’s first visit to Ceuta and Melilla as king brings Spain’s territorial dispute with Morocco back into focus.
articles.body:
Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia are due to visit Ceuta on October 13 and Melilla the following day, in Felipe’s first visit to either city as king since he ascended the throne in 2014.

The trip comes after a major migration crisis at the Ceuta border in July and as the long-running dispute between Spain and Morocco over the two cities on the North African coast remains unresolved.

Spain considers Ceuta and Melilla part of its territory, while Morocco regards both cities and several smaller Spanish-held territories in North Africa as part of its own territory.

The city that sits on the southern side of the Strait of Gibraltar also has different names in Spanish and Arabic.

In Spain, it is Ceuta. In Arabic, it is Sabta, commonly written as Sebta in Latin script.

So why does the same city have two names? And how did a city on the North African coast come under Spanish sovereignty?

The name is much older than either modern Spain or Morocco.

The city was known as Sabta in Arabic. Spain’s Ministry of Culture identifies Sabta with present-day Ceuta and traces its history through successive periods of Idrisid, Umayyad, Taifa, Almoravid, Almohad and Marinid rule.

The Spanish form, Ceuta, developed from earlier forms of the name. Sabta and Ceuta are different linguistic forms of the same city.

Ceuta passed through several political and dynastic systems in the Maghreb and al-Andalus.

Under the Idrisid dynasty, the city was in the hands of the Banu Isam before being taken by the Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Rahman III in 931, bringing it into the political sphere of al-Andalus.

In the 11th century, Ceuta became linked to the Taifa of Malaga. It later came under the Almoravids and Almohads. From the beginning of the 14th century, it became part of the Marinid sphere with periods when other local dynasties held power.

By the early 15th century, Ceuta was under Muslim rule.

On August 21, 1415, Portuguese forces led by King John I captured Ceuta.

The Portuguese conquest brought an end to more than seven centuries of Muslim rule in Ceuta. Ceuta’s own cultural heritage authority dates Muslim rule from 709 to the Portuguese conquest in 1415.

Ceuta remained Portuguese for more than two centuries.

Portugal and Spain were then ruled by the same monarchy from 1580 to 1640. When Portugal restored its independence in 1640, Ceuta remained under the Spanish monarchy rather than returning to Portuguese rule.

The 1668 Treaty of Lisbon, which formally recognised Portuguese independence, left Ceuta in Spanish hands.

That is how Ceuta came under Spanish sovereignty.

Morocco’s argument is rooted in the city’s history and geography.

Ceuta lies on the North African coast, surrounded by Morocco on its landward side. Morocco has claimed Ceuta and Melilla since gaining independence in 1956 and regards the two cities as occupied Moroccan territories.

Under Spanish law, Ceuta is an autonomous city. Its Statute of Autonomy describes Ceuta as an integral part of the Spanish nation and gives the city its own system of self-government.

The dispute, therefore, is not about who administers Ceuta. Spain does. It is about sovereignty.

Morocco says Ceuta should form part of Moroccan territory. Spain says its sovereignty over the city is established and Ceuta is part of Spain.

Neither side has accepted the other’s position.

Because the two sides interpret that history differently.

Morocco points to Ceuta’s long history within Muslim political systems in the Maghreb and its location on the North African coast. Spain points to centuries of Portuguese and Spanish control and to Ceuta’s present constitutional status as part of Spain.

The historical record does not provide a simple answer to a modern sovereignty dispute. The political systems that ruled Ceuta before 1415 were not nation-states with today’s borders, and the city’s current status is based on centuries of subsequent Portuguese and Spanish rule.

Morocco’s territorial claim dates from the period after independence in 1956, but Spain has continued to exercise sovereignty over Ceuta.

Sebta, or Sabta, is the Arabic name for Ceuta and predates the modern sovereignty dispute.

In Morocco, Sebta is the Arabic name used for the city while Ceuta is the established Spanish form.

The choice of name can have political resonance because Morocco disputes Spanish sovereignty over the city. But using Sebta is not automatically a political statement. It is also simply the Arabic name.

Melilla’s history is different from Ceuta’s.

Spanish forces took control of Melilla in 1497 when it was incorporated into the Crown of Castile.

Ceuta, by contrast, was first Portuguese before remaining under the Spanish monarchy after Portugal regained its independence.

Today, both cities are Spanish autonomous cities, and Morocco claims sovereignty over both.

Ceuta’s importance today goes beyond its size.

Ceuta is considered part of Spain, but it is not included in the European Union customs territory. Its border with Morocco is also an external border of the Schengen area.

That has made Ceuta a focal point for migration and border policy as well as a recurring issue in relations between Madrid and Rabat.

The issue returned sharply to the headlines on July 30 when more than 72,000 migrants entered Ceuta from Morocco, according to the Reuters news agency.

Now Felipe’s planned visits to Ceuta and Melilla are putting the two disputed cities back in the spotlight.

articles.title: Tom Emmer tells Jon Karl there are 'communists' on the midterm ballot in heated ABC exchange
articles.summary: House Majority Whip Tom Emmer clashed with Jon Karl on ABC's "This Week," insisting that Democratic socialists on the ballot are actually communists.
articles.body: House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., pushed back against ABC's "This Week" host Jon Karl after he insisted "there aren’t a lot of communists on the ballot" Sunday. The clash began after Emmer conceded the Republican Party needed to make an effort to lower gas prices ahead of the midterm elections. "I would say this on that, $4 gas, $6 diesel, entirely unacceptable," Emmer said. "We Republicans agree on that. But it’s not enough to vote for communists." "I think most Democrats would say they’re not communists," Karl replied with a chuckle. "So, there aren’t a lot of communists on the ballot in these midterms." SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES' "Well you’re wrong, they are communists," Emmer interrupted. Karl conceded that there were "some Democratic socialists" on the ballot and attempted to move on to a new topic, but Emmer rejected the idea. "Jon, you just called them what they want you to call them. There’s nothing Democratic about socialism. For 100 years, they wanted us to call them progressives, when, in fact, they were socialists. And it wasn’t cool to admit you’re a socialist. They are now communists and Marxists. Take a look at the [Democratic Socialists of America] platform," Emmer said. Karl again attempted to change topics, but Emmer continued. VULNERABLE DEMOCRAT WARNS PARTY TO 'FIGHT BACK' AGAINST GROWING SOCIALIST MOVEMENT "They want to defund the police. They want to defund prisons. They want government-only health care. And they want the Green New Deal, which will cost every American family another $355,000. That’s what we should be talking about," Emmer said. Earlier in the interview, Emmer also criticized mainstream media for framing inflation and high gas prices under President Donald Trump differently from how they reported them under former President Joe Biden. "I hate to point the finger at you and the other journalists, but have you reported that under Joe Biden, the average was over $5 a gallon? Under Donald Trump, he’s pulled it all the way back, even with the action that had to be taken to make sure that Iran never has a nuclear weapon. It’s closer to $4. It’s about 13 percent below what Joe Biden had. Grocery inflation. Under Biden, it was 13-point-something. Under Donald Trump, it’s two percent. It’s 11 points better. But you guys don’t report this stuff. So, I’m not saying the American people don’t get it. They don’t get the truth from the people that are reporting it," Emmer said. MORE AMERICANS THAN EVER NOW HAVE A POSITIVE VIEW OF SOCIALISM, NEW POLL SAYS Fox News Digital reached out to Emmer and ABC News for comment. Emmer made similar comments in an interview with Fox News Digital last week when he accused the far-left wing of the Democratic Party of being "communists, Marxists and anarchists." He especially took issue with Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, though he has denied being a socialist. "This guy says ridiculous things like U.S. NFL football is an example of toxic masculinity, he supports a terrorist who believes that America deserved to lose 3,000 people on 9/11, and he's got this Piker guy who's just shooting his mouth off on everything anti-American," Emmer said. "These people are anti-American more than anything else." articles.title: Hurricane Isaias leaves trail of destruction across the US Gulf Coast
articles.summary: Crews rally for massive cleanup effort in Florida and Alabama as Isaias leaves hundreds of thousands in the dark.
articles.body:
Residents across the southeastern United States have begun cleanup efforts after Hurricane Isaias , the first Atlantic tropical cyclone of the 2026 season, slammed ashore near Destin, Florida, on Friday.

As of midafternoon Sunday, roughly 356,000 customers remain without power in southern Alabama and the northwestern region of Florida, according to data from PowerOutage.com, an independent tracking website.

At its peak, the storm knocked out power to nearly 800,000 homes and businesses across the Gulf Coast.

Sarah Gatewood, a spokesperson for the utility company Florida Power and Light (FPL), announced that workers from across Florida and more than two dozen other states had mobilised to restore power.

At least four deaths have been linked to Isais after it made landfall as a Category 2 storm on the five-tier Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.

The tempest churned northward into Alabama on Saturday with fierce tropical-storm-force winds before weakening into a post-tropical cyclone and tracking further north towards the Appalachians.

Though its power is waning , the storm continues to endanger the mid-Atlantic region with the potential for flash flooding.

According to the National Weather Service (NWS), surface observations indicate that Isaias now has maximum sustained winds of 160 km/h (100 mph) and an estimated minimum central pressure of 28.88 inches, or 978 millibars.

Across Florida and Alabama, residents have reported damage from the storm’s high-velocity winds.

A Rest and Relax Inn in the resort city of Pensacola, Florida, saw its roof sheared off during the hurricane, and a boathouse was flattened in Destin.

The immediate struggle for basic necessities was most stark in Pensacola, the westernmost part of the Florida Panhandle, where the storm downed power grids and caused widespread structural damage.

Hundreds of cars lined the block around a United Cajun Navy distribution site, a volunteer disaster relief organisation, on Saturday morning.

Pensacola’s Mayor DC Reeves warned of critical drinking water shortages following the storm, which affected drinking wells and water infrastructure. Residents, he said, remain under an advisory to boil tap water before use.

“We are winding down day three of storm response and recovery operations, and we remain focused on public safety, clearing debris, and restoring critical infrastructure and services,” Reeves said on social media.

Isaias also forced the indefinite closure of Pensacola International airport, Florida’s 10th-largest airfield, due to severe damage.

Fallen trees and power lines continue to make travel hazardous in Houston County, Alabama, which remains under an emergency flash flood warning, according to state emergency officials.

“Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice,” the agency posted on X.

articles.title: Houthis kill 14 at Saudi airport as expert warns of 'rapid targets' amid Middle East war
articles.summary: Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi Arabian airports in Riyadh and Dammam, killing at least 14 and injuring over 300 as experts warn of wider war.
articles.body: Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports. The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector. The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300. SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis. "Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu, senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday. "The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned. RUBIO ACCUSES IRAN OF FLYING IRGC PERSONNEL INTO YEMEN AS HOUTHI THREAT ESCALATES The Houthis also renewed warnings Sunday, urging airlines, airport workers and travelers to avoid Saudi airports as Saudi Arabia vowed to retaliate for the deadly attacks. Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned Saturday's attack, confirming that an American was among those killed and calling for an immediate end to the violence. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, left open the possibility of U.S. involvement in Saudi Arabia's military campaign against the Houthis, saying, "We may. We're gonna look at it. We move very quickly." The escalation comes nearly three weeks after a senior Iranian official threatened to paralyze neighboring countries' airports if they cooperated with U.S. efforts to restrict Iranian flights. THE HOUTHIS AREN'T SOMEBODY ELSE'S PROBLEM. AMERICA CAN'T AFFORD TO LOOK AWAY Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned Sept. 23 that Iran would prevent neighboring countries' airports from operating if they cooperated with Washington's efforts to restrict Iranian flights, according to Reuters. "This rapid targeting reflects earlier threats made by Iranian officials, including a veiled threat from the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warning that U.S. sanctions on Iran's aviation sector would lead to retaliatory threats against neighboring aviation infrastructure," Taleblu said. Iran has long supported the Houthis, but the extent of Tehran's involvement in the latest airport attacks has not been independently established. The escalation has also renewed scrutiny of reports that Russia has provided intelligence and technical assistance to the Houthis. FOILED TERROR PLOT AT BOMBER BASE SIGNALS WIDER THREAT TO US MILITARY INSTALLATIONS: EXPERT At a Sept. 1 House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing , lawmakers pressed experts on allegations that Russia is providing intelligence and technical support to the Houthis. "Beyond offering diplomatic cover, there are persistent reports of Russian satellite collaboration, advisory support, and intelligence targeting assistance, as well as unproven allegations regarding select anti-ship systems." HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS But he also linked the latest attacks to a broader military escalation as the Houthis expand their territorial control in Yemen. "This surge did not occur in a vacuum," Taleblu said. "Since April, the Houthis have made territorial gains and pushed back against Saudi forces despite a period of diplomatic lull." articles.title: UK PM Andy Burnham says it is ‘clear’ Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
articles.summary: Claim marks the first time a UK prime minister has publicly acknowledged Russia’s interference in the vote to leave EU.
articles.body:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said it is “clear” that Russia interfered in the country’s 2016 Brexit vote, warning French and German voters of the same threat.

“I asked the question coming to Downing Street: Was there interference in the 2016 referendum from Russia? And I’ve had the clear answer that yes, there was,” Burnham said in an interview with The Rest Is Politics podcast released on Sunday.

Burnham’s comments mark the first time a UK prime minister has publicly acknowledged that Russia interfered in the UK’s vote to leave the European Union. Burnham did not provide evidence for or details on the claim.

He said that “these things are important now to put clearly on the record, and, I believe, help voters in Germany and France understand that some of this politics is instigated via our enemies, namely Russia.”

Burnham said he spoke with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz about possible links between Russia and the far-right Alternative for Germany party when the two leaders met last week in Berlin.

In his address to the United Nations General Assembly in September, Burnham also condemned Russia’s attempt to interfere in the UK’s 2019 general election.

According to a 2020 report by Parliament’s Intelligence and Security Committee, the UK government had failed to ask for a deep assessment of Russia’s interference in the 2016 referendum. The report did confirm that Russia had meddled in the 2014 Scottish independence referendum , however.

Russia has repeatedly denied meddling in Western democracies or interfering in another country’s elections or referendums, casting the UK as being gripped by “anti-Russian hysteria”.

Last month, Burnham argued that the UK should reconsider options for a future relationship with the EU, including rejoining the bloc, reigniting the decisive debate more than a decade after the historic vote.

He said that the UK’s departure from the bloc had failed to fulfil Brexit supporters’ pledge of “taking back control”, and instead has made the UK weaker economically and on immigration.

articles.title: Pennsylvania shooter who killed 8 was family’s patriarch, father of slain toddler says
articles.summary: Police said that the 45-year-old gunman was related to seven of the victims and that he took his own life.
articles.body: ERIE, Pa. — A man whose toddler was among eight people killed in a mass shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, said Sunday that the gunman was a grandfather who never seemed distressed or out of the ordinary. “I think that was a front for him,” Julius Windham said as he stood at a memorial to victims of Friday’s shooting, including his 1-year-old daughter Amarianna, her pregnant mother and the woman’s 5-year-old son and unborn baby. “Him every day, him smiling and being just — you would think of nothing like that would happen,” Windham said. The 45-year-old gunman took his own life. Authorities have not released his name, but Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said he was related to seven of the victims. The eighth was a friend of the pregnant woman, he said. Police have not made their names public, either. Those killed include 2 women outside the home Mourners on Sunday placed candles, flowers and stuffed animals outside the home where the man opened fire shortly before 5 p.m. Friday. Windham wore a T-shirt with pictures of the women and children and the words, “Forever In My Heart.” “Words can’t even explain what I’m going through right now,” Windham said. “But I gotta be strong for my community, you know what I’m saying? My family, my daughters, my sons, everybody.” Video and audio evidence recovered by investigators included muffled gunshot sounds coming from inside the home just before two “distressed” women arrived and began pounding on the door, Lorah said. The gunman then came out and shot them as they ran toward him, before returning inside. Responding officers found the two women dead outside. After deploying a drone and robot, they went inside and found the bodies of the 5-year-old boy and 1-year-old girl on the first floor; two more women and two young men in a stairwell; and the shooter on the second floor. “Out of respect for the victims and the families, I will not discuss the details of what our officers encountered inside that home,” the chief said at a news conference. “But I want our community to understand the gravity of what happened and the profound impact this tragedy has had on those involved and on our community as a whole,” he said. Police decline to discuss motive as investigation continues Erie is about 120 miles north of Pittsburgh. Lorah declined to discuss motive but suggested mental health could be a factor. He said investigators would talk to relatives and examine the cellphones of the women who were killed outside the home. “They knew something was going on at that house,” Lorah said. “We have to figure out what that is.” Nicole and Debra Eller, whose best friend was among the victims, said they’ve known the family for more than 30 years. Nicole Eller said the shooter “was a good guy, and then he started going downhill with everything.” “They were a lovely family. Who would have thought this would ever happen?” Debra Eller said. “Oh, my gosh, this is so upsetting. This should have never happened to her or the kids or anybody. His grandchildren, his kids, how can you do that?” The Erie shooting was reminiscent of a 1982 massacre in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, in which a man killed 13 people, including five of his own children. At a news conference Saturday, Erie Mayor Daria Devlin addressed a portion of her remarks directly to the victims’ families. “I am so deeply sorry,” Devlin said. “What happened to you was horrific, and there is nothing that any of us can say today that will make this any easier. ... Our entire community is with you, we’re grieving with you. And we are here to support you.” If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

articles.title: Flash flood hits northern Nepal, damaging bridges and sweeping away homes
articles.summary: Residents along the Budhi Gandaki river in north central Nepal evacuated on Sunday as flash flooding destroyed homes and other structures in the area.
articles.body: KATHMANDU, Nepal — Residents along the Budhi Gandaki River in north-central Nepal evacuated on Sunday as flash flooding destroyed homes and other structures in the area. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority evacuated villagers and warned others to move to safer areas while remaining on alert until late Sunday. The agency said at least five people are reported missing so far. The flash flood also damaged or destroyed four bridges, swept away about three dozen houses and damaged the construction site of a hydropower plant. Several power and communication towers were also damaged along the riverside. Nepal’s army said in a statement that it was continuing to rescue stranded people using helicopters and ground troops. They had rescued 49 people by Sunday afternoon. The agency said the flash flood was caused by a landslide that initially blocked the Budhi Gangaki River near the village of Chumchure. The dam formed by the landslide breached, triggering the flood. The Budhi Gandaki River merges into the Trishuli River and is a key waterway near the capital, Kathmandu. Videos on social media show houses and sheds being swept away by the swollen river flowing between tall mountains. It was not immediately clear how many of the small villages in the mountainous area were affected. Social media posts indicate the government warning prompted an evacuation in Arughat, a riverside town on the highway connecting Kathmandu to other parts of the country. Nepal is still recovering from a devastating flood in August along the mountainous Nepal-China border that left more than 1,400 people dead and thousands more missing. The office of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Monday announced an end to search-and-rescue operations for additional victims. Authorities will instead concentrate on recovery, including restoration of roads and bridges cut off by floods, particularly in remote areas where damaged infrastructure has made aid deliveries difficult. The government estimates the rebuilding effort will cost $4.77 billion. Nearly 33,000 people have been affected and about 7,500 homes were damaged or destroyed.

articles.title: Flash flood sweeps away 40 houses, 6 bridges in Nepal; up to 10 missing
articles.summary: A pre-dawn flash flood in Nepal’s Manaslu trekking region on Sunday swept away nearly 40 houses, six bridges and hydropower infrastructure.
articles.body: A pre-dawn flash flood in Nepal’s Manaslu trekking region on Sunday swept away nearly 40 houses, six bridges and hydropower infrastructure. Up to 10 people are missing and more than 150 foreign tourists are stranded.Early SMS warnings helped residents flee to higher ground, while the Army rescued 49 people. Authorities ordered evacuations and alerted downstream districts.The disaster struck barely 45 days after catastrophic floods along Bhote Koshi-Trishuli river killed more than 1,450 people and left 5,250 missing. The latest flood struck around 4am along Budhi Gandaki, a tributary of Trishuli, in Chumnubri, approximately 100km west of Kathmandu.100+ foreigners stuck in trekking regionAuthorities suspected a landslide had temporarily blocked a tributary, allowing water and debris to build up before the obstruction gave way. However, officials had yet to establish the exact cause. Five people, including two women and three men staying near Ungilung river, remained missing. Separately, four to five herders were also out of contact.The flood destroyed 35-40 houses and a primary school, leaving another 20-22 houses at risk. articles.title: At least 139 migrants dead, 84 missing after overcrowded boat capsizes off Djibouti
articles.summary: More than 80 people survived the deadly crossing from Djibouti toward Yemen, while at least 84 remained missing as authorities worked to verify additional victims.
articles.body: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died when a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the United Nations' migration agency. The vessel was carrying 305 people from Djibouti toward Yemen when it capsized Thursday night or early Friday near Guhere, north of Obock, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Sunday. At least 84 people remained missing as of Sunday, while more than 80 survived. All of the survivors were Ethiopian nationals, according to the agency. "No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way," IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a statement. DRAMATIC FOOTAGE SHOWS ALLEGED NARCO BOAT ERUPT IN FIREBALL DURING US MILITARY STRIKE "We cannot keep treating these deaths as normal. Safe and legal pathways save lives. I am asking governments and donors to act before the next boat goes down," Pope added. The confirmed death toll includes only victims buried by authorities in Djibouti and could rise as additional bodies are verified, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac told The Associated Press. Some victims were buried by fellow migrants but will not be added to the official count until authorities can verify the bodies, the outlet reported. BOATER WAS DRUNK, DANCING BEFORE BOSTON HARBOR CRASH THAT KILLED 24-YEAR-OLD FORMER SOCCER PLAYER, DA SAYS "What is terrible is that they were buried with no names, in a common grave, like in a war situation," Coissac said. "They all have a mother, a father, and we may never learn what happened." Coissac said the boat sank shortly after departing on the evening of Oct. 8, "mainly because it was overcrowded." Survivors were taken to an IOM rescue center in Obock, where they were receiving medical treatment after swallowing seawater as well as psychological support, according to The Associated Press. FEDERAL AGENTS INTERCEPT BOAT CARRYING 14 ILLEGAL ALIENS BEFORE UNLOADING IN WEALTHY COASTAL ENCLAVE "They're all in a state of shock," Coissac said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The crossing from the Horn of Africa to the Arabian Peninsula is a common but dangerous route for migrants seeking work in Gulf countries. More than 900 migrants died or went missing along the route last year, according to the IOM. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles, the latest in a streak of weapons tests
articles.summary: South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff didn’t immediately specify how many missiles were detected or how far they flew.
articles.body: SEOUL, South Korea — North Korea on Monday fired multiple ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters, South Korea’s military said, adding to a recent streak of weapons demonstrations that has heightened tensions during a prolonged freeze in diplomacy. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were fired from an area around the North Korean capital of Pyongyang, where the country has used its airport as a major launch site in recent years. The joint chiefs did not immediately specify how many missiles they detected or how far they flew. Japan’s Defense Ministry said it detected at least two missiles and assessed that the weapons landed in waters outside the country’s exclusive economic zone. The launch came days after South Korea on Friday flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon, designed to fly at least five times the speed of sound and evade missile defense systems, which President Lee Jae Myung described as an important step in strengthening the South’s conventional defense capabilities. While maintaining a hard line toward Seoul, North Korea has been ramping up weapons testing as it seeks to expand its arsenal of nuclear-capable systems, including an Oct. 3 test of what the North described as a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to evade missile defenses in South Korea and Japan. North Korea has also conducted other missile tests and live-fire drills and commissioned a new warship as leader Kim Jong Un continues to flaunt his nuclear weapons program while rejecting U.S. and South Korean offers to resume long-stalled diplomacy. Tensions were further worsened after three South Korean soldiers were injured in land mine explosions last month near the heavily armed inter-Korean border. The South’s military and the U.S.-led United Nations Command concluded the blasts were caused by devices planted by North Korea, which has denied responsibility and ridiculed the South’s demands for an apology. Kim in recent years has halted all diplomacy and cooperation with South Korea and described the neighbor as a permanent enemy during a prolonged stalemate in larger nuclear negotiations with Washington. He has so far rebuffed U.S. President Donald Trump’s calls to revive their diplomacy, which broke down in 2019, with his government demanding that Washington abandon its “hostile” policy toward Pyongyang and drop demands for North Korea’s denuclearization as a precondition for talks. The tensions have been a setback for Lee, who favors engagement with North Korea and has tempered his rhetoric toward the North even as public anger grows over the mine blasts. Lee has also called for strengthening South Korea’s conventional defense capabilities while reducing its reliance on the United States. Washington unilaterally decided to scale back a major military exercise with South Korea in August, with Trump citing his “very good relationship” with Kim.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says 1 dead, 11 injured in latest attack on Riyadh airport
articles.summary: Sunday’s strike on King Khalid International airport kills a Pakistani national.
articles.body:
A projectile has struck Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International airport, killing one person and injuring 11, according to the country’s civil aviation authority.

The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) identified the deceased in Sunday’s attack as a Pakistani resident and said the injured were transferred to several hospitals for medical care.

The strike on terminals 3 and 4, which serve domestic flights, occurred a day after a Houthi missile hit the airport, killing 12 people and wounding more than 300, according to the Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

India’s embassy in Saudi Arabia said one of its citizens died on Sunday due to injuries sustained in Saturday’s attack, bringing the death toll to 13.

Following Sunday’s attack, GACA said damage assessments and safety inspections of the airport were under way.

A witness on board a taxiing aircraft at the airport told the Reuters news agency that a projectile struck the tarmac next to several parked planes at about 8:30pm (17:30 GMT) on Sunday, causing a fire.

The witness said the aircraft returned to the gate, where the passengers disembarked and were told to leave.

The Riyadh airport has been struck four times in the past five days. Houthi attacks on King Khalid airport on Thursday killed at least three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, according to GACA.

The airport has been closed since Saturday’s attack, which was the deadliest in the country since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February.

The Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes before Sunday’s.

The airport attacks have escalated the war in Yemen and threaten to draw in the US military. US President Donald Trump says he is weighing whether to join the fight against the Houthis.

The escalation puts further pressure on global oil supplies and prices, as well as on commercial shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb strait off the Yemeni coast, a crucial alternative waterway to the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump had said he intends to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who is seeking help against the Houthis, but there were no signs on Sunday that the US president had followed up on his claim.

There are fears that US intervention could prompt the Houthis to halt shipping through Bab al-Mandeb, further restricting the flow of oil out of the Gulf.

The rebels seized key areas along the strait last month. The Saudi-led coalition, backing forces loyal to Yemen’s internationally recognised government, has been trying to seize them back.

articles.title: Maduro-linked fugitive nabbed over alleged scheme to cash in on Venezuelans’ basic needs
articles.summary: Alvaro Pulido Vargas allegedly exploited Venezuela's CLAP food program and housing contracts, funneling billions through U.S. banks to hide bribes.
articles.body: A fugitive accused of getting rich off programs meant to help Venezuelans is now in U.S. custody, facing charges in a sprawling corruption scandal tied to Nicolás Maduro’s regime. Alvaro Pulido Vargas, 62, was arrested during a Homeland Security Task Force operation and is scheduled to appear Tuesday, Oct. 13, in federal court in South Florida, the Justice Department announced. The Colombian national faces two criminal cases alleging he helped funnel money from Venezuelan government bribery schemes through U.S. banks to hide illicit profits. NICOLAS MADURO AND WIFE CILIA FLORES FACE NEW CHARGE OF CONSPIRACY TO TORTURE AMERICANS "Pulido is charged in two separate, significant money laundering schemes, both using the U.S. financial system to hide the profits from his bribery and greed off the backs of the Venezuelan people," said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva. Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the arrest Sunday on X, accusing Pulido Vargas of exploiting programs meant to provide essential supplies and housing. "His alleged actions show a blatant disregard to the Venezuelan people by corrupting government programs intended to provide critical food, medicine, and housing for personal enrichment and exploiting the American financial system to do it," Blanche wrote. Pulido Vargas, also known as German Enrique Rubio Salas, was charged in 2019 and again in 2021. The Justice Department said he previously was convicted of drug trafficking in Italy in 1997 under that alias. "For years, DEA and our HSTF partners have pursued Pulido Vargas across borders. Today, that pursuit has brought him to the Southern District of Florida," DEA Administrator Terrance Cole said. The newer case centers on approximately $1.6 billion in Venezuelan government contracts to supply food and medicine through CLAP, a government-run distribution program. OUR ADVERSARIES ARE EVEN USING THE US BANKING SYSTEM. HERE’S HOW THEY GET AWAY WITH IT Prosecutors say Pulido Vargas and his associates paid bribes to win the contracts, then inflated prices to cover the payoffs and line their own pockets. The alleged scheme ran from approximately July 2015 through at least 2020. His son, Emmanuel Enrique Rubio Gonzalez, and former Venezuelan state governor Jose Gregorio Vielma-Mora were among four others charged in the case. NICOLÁS MADURO AND HIS WIFE EXPECTED TO FACE NEW CHARGES RELATED TO ALLEGED TORTURE OF AMERICANS Prosecutors say Vielma-Mora and a middleman collected roughly $17.3 million in bribes and illicit payments for helping steer government food contracts and other business advantages to the group. The money allegedly flowed through a web of companies and bank accounts in Antigua, the United Arab Emirates, the United States and elsewhere. The 2021 indictment describes fake contracts and other paperwork allegedly used to make the payments appear legitimate. Approximately $180 million moved through or into the United States, including accounts in South Florida, according to prosecutors. "The allegations describe a profound betrayal of the Venezuelan people; corrupting government programs intended to provide critical food, medicine, and housing for personal enrichment," said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones. MADURO CLAIMS IMMUNITY, ASKS JUDGE TO DISMISS DRUG-TRAFFICKING CHARGES AGAINST HIM AND HIS WIFE The earlier case centers on an alleged scheme to cash in on a government program meant to build homes for low-income Venezuelans. Prosecutors charged Pulido Vargas and Maduro ally Alex Nain Saab Moran in 2019, accusing them of using a housing contract to exploit Venezuela’s government-controlled currency exchange system. NICOLÁS MADURO FLASHES PEACE SIGNS IN FIRST PRISON PHOTOS SINCE US CAPTURE IN CARACAS The men allegedly submitted false paperwork claiming they had imported goods and building materials that never entered Venezuela, then bribed officials to approve those documents. Prosecutors say they moved approximately $350 million out of Venezuela through U.S. banks and into overseas accounts they controlled. The alleged scheme ran from approximately November 2011 through at least September 2015. Pulido Vargas faces five money laundering-related charges in the 2021 case, each carrying a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison. He faces eight additional money laundering-related charges in the 2019 case. The DEA, FBI and Homeland Security Investigations are investigating the cases through the Homeland Security Task Force initiative. Blanche pointed to the arrest as a warning to others facing U.S. prosecution. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "No amount of time or distance will stop @TheJusticeDept from working with our federal law enforcement and international partners to pursue these criminals and bring them to justice in an American courtroom," he wrote.

articles.title: 2 Renoir paintings recovered from French museum heist, 6 arrested
articles.summary: Two Renoir paintings stolen from a museum in southern France last month have been found, and six people arrested, local authorities said Friday.
articles.body: Two Renoir paintings stolen from a museum in southern France last month have been found, and six people arrested, local authorities said Friday. The mayor of the town housing the Renoir Museum, Bryan Masson, issued a statement praising investigators who tracked down the paintings and suspects. The statement did not elaborate on how they did so. The regional prosecutor’s office and police did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The mayor announced a news conference for later Friday. The two missing paintings were “Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano” and “Young Woman at the Well.” The thieves sliced through a fence, climbed through a window and initially stole four valuable Renoir paintings in the heist last month, but abandoned two of the artworks as they fled, authorities said. Investigators launched a national search for the perpetrators. The whole operation took less than three minutes and targeted the most valuable works in the Renoir Museum in the town of Cagnes-sur-Mer, the regional prosecutor’s office said. The theft conjured up painful memories of the spectacular heist of crown jewels at the Louvre Museum in Paris last year and revived calls for better security and better funding for the many cultural sites large and small that dot France’s landscape.
